name: Aloo Curry
ingredients:
4 medium Potatoes, chopped
2 medium Onions, finely chopped
1 tbsp Ginger-Garlic Paste
2 medium Tomatoes, pureed or chopped
2-3 Green Chilies, slit
1 tsp Cumin Seeds
1/2 tsp Turmeric Powder
1 tsp Red Chili Powder
1 tsp Garam Masala
2 tbsp Oil or Ghee
Salt to taste
2 tbsp Fresh Coriander Leaves, chopped
instructions_en:
1. Preparation: Thoroughly wash and prepare Aloo. If it's meat or paneer, marinate it with a little turmeric, red chili powder, salt, and lemon juice for 20 minutes. Finely chop 2 onions and puree 2 tomatoes.
2. Whole Spices (Tadka): Heat 3 tbsp of oil or ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan or pressure cooker over medium heat. Add cumin seeds, 1 bay leaf, 2-3 cloves, and a small cinnamon stick. Let them sizzle for 30 seconds to release their aroma.
3. Onion Base: Add the finely chopped onions and a pinch of salt. Sauté patiently for 8-10 minutes until they turn a deep golden brown.
4. Aromatics & Tomatoes: Add 1 tbsp of ginger-garlic paste and green chilies. Sauté for 1 minute until the raw smell goes away. Pour in the tomato puree and cook until the mixture thickens and oil starts separating from the edges (about 5-7 minutes).
5. Spice Powders: Lower the heat and add 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, and 1/2 tsp cumin powder. Stir constantly for 30 seconds so the spices bloom without burning.
6. Adding Base: Add the prepared Aloo to the masala. Sauté on medium-high heat for 4-5 minutes to coat everything well and seal in the flavors.
7. Simmering: Pour in 1 to 1.5 cups of warm water (adjust for desired gravy consistency). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover with a lid, and simmer. Cook until the Aloo is completely tender (15 mins for veg/paneer, 30-45 mins for meat).
8. Final Garnish: Crush 1 tsp of Kasuri Methi (dried fenugreek leaves) between your palms and sprinkle it over the curry along with 1/2 tsp of garam masala. Garnish with freshly chopped cilantro and serve hot.

name: Aloo Fry
ingredients:
4 medium Potatoes, chopped
2 medium Onions, finely chopped
1 tbsp Ginger-Garlic Paste
2 medium Tomatoes, pureed or chopped
2-3 Green Chilies, slit
1 tsp Cumin Seeds
1/2 tsp Turmeric Powder
1 tsp Red Chili Powder
1 tsp Garam Masala
2 tbsp Oil or Ghee
Salt to taste
2 tbsp Fresh Coriander Leaves, chopped
instructions_en:
1. Ingredient Prep: Wash, peel, and chop Aloo into even, bite-sized pieces. Finely chop onions, tomatoes, and slit green chilies.
2. Tempering (Tadka): Heat 2-3 tbsp of oil (mustard oil preferred for vegetables) in a wide pan. Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, a pinch of hing (asafoetida), and curry leaves. Let them splutter.
3. Aromatics: Add chopped onions and sauté until translucent. Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté for another minute.
4. Main Ingredient Addition: Add the chopped Aloo along with a pinch of turmeric and salt. Mix well to coat with the oil and spices.
5. Searing/Cooking: Cook uncovered on medium-high heat for the first 5 minutes to get a slight sear. Then, reduce the heat, cover with a lid, and cook until Aloo is 80% tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
6. Spicing: Remove the lid and add dry spice powders (coriander powder, cumin powder, red chili powder, amchur/dry mango powder). Mix thoroughly.
7. Finishing: Sauté on medium heat for another 3-4 minutes to crisp up the edges. Finish with a sprinkle of garam masala and fresh coriander leaves. Serve hot as a side dish.

8. Final Garnish: Crush 1 tsp of Kasuri Methi (dried fenugreek leaves) between your palms and sprinkle it over the curry along with 1/2 tsp of garam masala. Garnish with freshly chopped cilantro and serve hot.

6. Adding Base: Add the prepared Fish to the masala. Sauté on medium-high heat for 4-5 minutes to coat everything well and seal in the flavors.

8. Final Garnish: Crush 1 tsp of Kasuri Methi (dried fenugreek leaves) between your palms and sprinkle it over the curry along with 1/2 tsp of garam masala. Garnish with freshly chopped cilantro and serve hot.

name: Prawn Korma
ingredients:

1 tsp Cumin Seeds
1/2 tsp Turmeric Powder
1 tsp Red Chili Powder
1 tsp Garam Masala
2 tbsp Oil or Ghee
Salt to taste
2 tbsp Fresh Coriander Leaves, chopped
instructions_en:
1. Preparation: Thoroughly wash and prepare Prawn. If it's meat or paneer, marinate it with a little turmeric, red chili powder, salt, and lemon juice for 20 minutes. Finely chop 2 onions and puree 2 tomatoes.
2. Whole Spices (Tadka): Heat 3 tbsp of oil or ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan or pressure cooker over medium heat. Add cumin seeds, 1 bay leaf, 2-3 cloves, and a small cinnamon stick. Let them sizzle for 30 seconds to release their aroma.
3. Onion Base: Add the finely chopped onions and a pinch of salt. Sauté patiently for 8-10 minutes until they turn a deep golden brown.
4. Aromatics & Tomatoes: Add 1 tbsp of ginger-garlic paste and green chilies. Sauté for 1 minute until the raw smell goes away. Pour in the tomato puree and cook until the mixture thickens and oil starts separating from the edges (about 5-7 minutes).
5. Spice Powders: Lower the heat and add 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, and 1/2 tsp cumin powder. Stir constantly for 30 seconds so the spices bloom without burning.
6. Adding Base: Add the prepared Prawn to the masala. Sauté on medium-high heat for 4-5 minutes to coat everything well and seal in the flavors.
7. Simmering: Pour in 1 to 1.5 cups of warm water (adjust for desired gravy consistency). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover with a lid, and simmer. Cook until the Prawn is completely tender (15 mins for veg/paneer, 30-45 mins for meat).
8. Final Garnish: Crush 1 tsp of Kasuri Methi (dried fenugreek leaves) between your palms and sprinkle it over the curry along with 1/2 tsp of garam masala. Garnish with freshly chopped cilantro and serve hot.

name: Keema Korma

1 tsp Garam Masala

Salt to taste
2 tbsp Fresh Coriander Leaves, chopped
instructions_en:
1. Preparation: Thoroughly wash and prepare Keema. If it's meat or paneer, marinate it with a little turmeric, red chili powder, salt, and lemon juice for 20 minutes. Finely chop 2 onions and puree 2 tomatoes.
2. Whole Spices (Tadka): Heat 3 tbsp of oil or ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan or pressure cooker over medium heat. Add cumin seeds, 1 bay leaf, 2-3 cloves, and a small cinnamon stick. Let them sizzle for 30 seconds to release their aroma.
3. Onion Base: Add the finely chopped onions and a pinch of salt. Sauté patiently for 8-10 minutes until they turn a deep golden brown.
4. Aromatics & Tomatoes: Add 1 tbsp of ginger-garlic paste and green chilies. Sauté for 1 minute until the raw smell goes away. Pour in the tomato puree and cook until the mixture thickens and oil starts separating from the edges (about 5-7 minutes).
5. Spice Powders: Lower the heat and add 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, and 1/2 tsp cumin powder. Stir constantly for 30 seconds so the spices bloom without burning.
6. Adding Base: Add the prepared Keema to the masala. Sauté on medium-high heat for 4-5 minutes to coat everything well and seal in the flavors.
7. Simmering: Pour in 1 to 1.5 cups of warm water (adjust for desired gravy consistency). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover with a lid, and simmer. Cook until the Keema is completely tender (15 mins for veg/paneer, 30-45 mins for meat).
8. Final Garnish: Crush 1 tsp of Kasuri Methi (dried fenugreek leaves) between your palms and sprinkle it over the curry along with 1/2 tsp of garam masala. Garnish with freshly chopped cilantro and serve hot.

name: Plain Roti
ingredients:
2 cups Whole Wheat Flour (Atta) or Maida
Water as needed for kneading
instructions_en:
1. Dough Preparation: In a large mixing bowl, combine flour (wheat or maida), a pinch of salt, and 1 tbsp oil/ghee. Gradually add warm water and knead into a soft, smooth dough. Cover with a damp cloth and let it rest for 30 minutes.
2. Portioning: Divide the rested dough into equal-sized lemon balls. Roll them smooth between your palms.
3. Rolling: Dust a dough ball with dry flour and roll it out into an even circle using a rolling pin (approx 6-inch diameter).
4. Cooking Preparation: Heat a tawa (flat griddle) on medium-high heat. Once hot, place the rolled Plain Roti on the tawa.
5. First Flip: Cook until small bubbles start to form on the surface (about 30-40 seconds), then flip it over.
6. Second Side & Puffing: Cook the other side for another 40 seconds until light brown spots appear. If making a paratha, apply ghee/oil on both sides and press gently with a spatula to crisp. If making roti, put directly on flame to puff up.
7. Serving: Remove from heat, brush lightly with butter or ghee, and store in an insulated container to keep soft. Serve hot.

name: Plain Biryani
ingredients:
2 cups Basmati Rice
2-3 Green Chilies, slit
1 tsp Cumin Seeds
1/2 tsp Turmeric Powder
1 tsp Red Chili Powder
1 tsp Garam Masala
2 tbsp Oil or Ghee
Salt to taste
2 tbsp Fresh Coriander Leaves, chopped
instructions_en:
1. Rice Soaking: Wash basmati rice 3-4 times until the water runs clear. Soak the rice in fresh water for 30 minutes, then drain completely.
2. Whole Spices (Temper): Heat 2 tbsp ghee or oil in a heavy-bottomed pot or pressure cooker. Add whole spices (bay leaf, cloves, green cardamom, cinnamon stick, cumin seeds) and let them crackle for a few seconds.
3. Aromatics: Add thinly sliced onions and sauté until they turn golden brown and caramelized. Add 1 tbsp of freshly pounded ginger-garlic paste and sauté until the raw smell disappears.
4. Base Addition: Add Rice, chopped tomatoes, green chilies, mint, and coriander leaves. Mix in dry spices (turmeric, red chili, biryani/pulao masala) and yogurt. Cook for 5-7 minutes until the oil starts separating.
5. Combining Rice: Gently fold in the soaked and drained rice. Stir delicately for 2 minutes so the grains are coated with the spiced ghee without breaking.
6. Liquid & Seasoning: Pour in hot water (standard ratio is 1.5 cups water for 1 cup rice). Season generously with salt. Bring the mixture to a rolling boil.
7. Dum (Steaming): Cover the pot tightly with a lid (seal with dough if possible). Lower the heat to the absolute minimum and cook for 15-20 minutes.
8. Resting & Serving: Turn off the heat and let it rest undisturbed for 10 minutes. Fluff gently with a fork, garnish with fried onions (birista) and fresh coriander, and serve hot with raita.

2 medium Onions, finely chopped
1 tbsp Ginger-Garlic Paste
2 medium Tomatoes, pureed or chopped
2-3 Green Chilies, slit
1 tsp Cumin Seeds
1/2 tsp Turmeric Powder
1 tsp Red Chili Powder
1 tsp Garam Masala
2 tbsp Oil or Ghee
Salt to taste
2 tbsp Fresh Coriander Leaves, chopped
instructions_en:
1. Rice Soaking: Wash basmati rice 3-4 times until the water runs clear. Soak the rice in fresh water for 30 minutes, then drain completely.
2. Whole Spices (Temper): Heat 2 tbsp ghee or oil in a heavy-bottomed pot or pressure cooker. Add whole spices (bay leaf, cloves, green cardamom, cinnamon stick, cumin seeds) and let them crackle for a few seconds.
3. Aromatics: Add thinly sliced onions and sauté until they turn golden brown and caramelized. Add 1 tbsp of freshly pounded ginger-garlic paste and sauté until the raw smell disappears.
4. Base Addition: Add Rice, chopped tomatoes, green chilies, mint, and coriander leaves. Mix in dry spices (turmeric, red chili, biryani/pulao masala) and yogurt. Cook for 5-7 minutes until the oil starts separating.
5. Combining Rice: Gently fold in the soaked and drained rice. Stir delicately for 2 minutes so the grains are coated with the spiced ghee without breaking.
6. Liquid & Seasoning: Pour in hot water (standard ratio is 1.5 cups water for 1 cup rice). Season generously with salt. Bring the mixture to a rolling boil.
7. Dum (Steaming): Cover the pot tightly with a lid (seal with dough if possible). Lower the heat to the absolute minimum and cook for 15-20 minutes.
8. Resting & Serving: Turn off the heat and let it rest undisturbed for 10 minutes. Fluff gently with a fork, garnish with fried onions (birista) and fresh coriander, and serve hot with raita.

4. Base Addition: Add Rice, chopped tomatoes, green chilies, mint, and coriander leaves. Mix in dry spices (turmeric, red chili, biryani/pulao masala) and yogurt. Cook for 5-7 minutes until the oil starts separating.

6. Liquid & Seasoning: Pour in hot water (standard ratio is 1.5 cups water for 1 cup rice). Season generously with salt. Bring the mixture to a rolling boil.
7. Dum (Steaming): Cover the pot tightly with a lid (seal with dough if possible). Lower the heat to the absolute minimum and cook for 15-20 minutes.
8. Resting & Serving: Turn off the heat and let it rest undisturbed for 10 minutes. Fluff gently with a fork, garnish with fried onions (birista) and fresh coriander, and serve hot with raita.
